newsitem.title: HONG KONG: AsiaSat resumes insurance claim talks.
newsitem.headline: AsiaSat resumes insurance claim talks.

text.p: Asia Satellite Telecommunications Co Ltd said on Monday it would resume negotiations this week on a US$58 million insurance claim for a power glitch in the highest-powered satellite over the region, AsiaSat2.
The claim is the maximum possible for a power reduction problem which the Hong Kong-based satellite operator believes occurred during the launch of AsiaSat2 late last year.
"We are hoping the claim can be resolved this month," Sabrina Cubbon, AsiaSat's general manager for marketing, told Reuters.
"Negotiations have started and will resume this week. We hope to now sit down with our insurance companies and negotiate from there," she said.
AsiaSat2, launched last November and placed in service in January, covers two-thirds of the world's population.

"Obviously it (the power reduction glitch) has caused problems because we'd have liked a perfect satellite," Cubbon said. "We wanted the best in Asia. Okay it's not a Rolls-Royce but it's still a BMW."
AsiaSat3 is due to be delivered into orbit in January, 1998.
